clue.text: He gave RUC trouble — a foreign minister?

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone made trouble for the Royal Ulster Constabulary: perhaps an overseas politician?
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges HE GAVE RUC into CHEGUEVAR, and the A completes the name. The question mark flags that this revolutionary is an unusual example of a minister: he held office in Cuba.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine-born revolutionary served as Cuba's minister of industries, a minister from abroad.

clue.text: Help I needed with top hamper

parts.note: to lend a hand is to help
a cap is a top, as on a bottle

explanation.surface: A request for help with a hamper whose lid is stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper someone is to hinder them, putting them at a disadvantage.

clue.text: Sentimentality is not all right

indicators.note: not all of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: something all right is good

explanation.surface: A complaint that mawkish feeling is unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all' tells you to shorten GOOD (all right) by its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is slang for cloying sentiment, sticky emotional mush.

clue.text: Unlimited number in major incident

indicators.note: without limits means the outer letters of the word go

parts.note: seventy is a number

explanation.surface: A count without bounds features in a serious emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlimited' strips the first and last letters, S and Y, from SEVENTY.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence of note, a significant happening.

clue.text: Pull up vehicle during a series of races 0

indicators.note: one piece occurring during another sits inside it

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man's series of motorcycle races

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone stops their car in the middle of a motor-racing festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull up' looks like one phrase, but 'Pull' is the definition and 'up' the reversal signal; 'during' is the container. The stray '0' at the end is an OCR artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull people in is to attract them; both mean draw towards.

clue.text: Engineer aims to hold organised rally in plant

indicators.note: one piece holding another contains it
to engineer is to contrive or rework, so these letters are rearranged
organised means put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone engineering a garden display includes a planned gathering among the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' and 'organised' are both anagram signals; 'to hold' is the container, so the rearranged rally sits inside the rearranged aims.
explanation.definitionFit: The amaryllis is a bulb grown for its large trumpet-shaped flowers.

clue.text: Team changing direction at kick-off gets off the mark

indicators.note: the opening letter, a compass point, is swapped for another compass point

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: A football team switches ends at the start and then scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing direction at kick-off' swaps the first letter S (south) for W (west). 'Off the mark' in the surface means to start scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot that is wide misses its target, so it is inaccurate.

clue.text: Go round town to get gardening aid

parts.note: to wheel is to turn round in a circle
Barrow-in-Furness is a town in Cumbria, England

explanation.surface: Advice to tour a town to find something for the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheelbarrow is a one-wheeled cart used for carrying loads in gardens.

clue.text: Take gamble about lines'to produce theatrical effect

indicators.note: one piece about another goes around it

parts.note: to dice is to take a gamble
RY, short for railway, is lines

explanation.surface: Advice to bet on some lines to create a stage illusion.
explanation.walkthrough: RY is the crossword convention for railway (lines). 'about' puts DICE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry ice, solid carbon dioxide, is used on stage to make low-lying fog.

clue.text: Feature of Wellington, not heartless but disrespectful

parts.note: a Wellington boot has an insole inside it

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

explanation.surface: A trait of the Duke of Wellington: not unkind, just rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wellington' suggests the Duke; it is the rubber boot. 'heartless' takes the middle O from NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent behaviour is rude and shows a lack of respect.

clue.text: Primate's main way of expressing agreement

definitions.meaning: a Madagascan lemur with long fingers, the clue's 's standing for is
the sailor's reply to an order at sea, the main being the sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the old poetic word for the sea, so this is how sailors agree.
explanation.definitionFit: The aye-aye is a nocturnal lemur; 'aye aye' is a naval acknowledgement meaning yes.

clue.text: Recalling order, I book accommodation for the men

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: to tell someone to do something is to order it

explanation.surface: An officer, remembering an instruction, reserves rooms for the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalling' reverses TELL + I + B to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet is lodging for soldiers, often in a private house.

clue.text: In part of The Office, contemptible Gareth finally turns sour

parts.note: little can mean petty or mean-spirited

indicators.note: finally means only the word's last letter is used
turns means the letters are changed round

explanation.surface: Within the TV sitcom, the despised Gareth ends up becoming bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Office' looks like the TV comedy with Gareth; it is the Divine Office, the Church's daily round of prayers. 'turns' is the anagram signal; 'finally' takes Gareth's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The little hours are the minor daytime services, such as Terce, Sext and None, in the Church's daily prayer cycle.

clue.text: Nowhere specific in America — Times Square, perhaps

definitions.meaning: American usage for wherever at all
read as a New York location, with NY for New York

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as A NY PLACE: Times Square is one spot in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyplace is the American form of anywhere, meaning no particular location.

clue.text: Hit the road after making a bundle down under

definitions.text: Hit the road after making a bundle down under

parts.words: Hit the road after making a bundle down under
parts.note: an Australian swagman rolls up his bundle of belongings and sets off tramping

explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a bundle' suggests getting rich; here it is packing a swag in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang the phrase means to travel on foot carrying one's swag, the rolled bundle called a matilda.

clue.text: Force change that's temporary

parts.note: to make someone do something is to force them
a shift is a change

explanation.surface: A forced alteration that is only stopgap.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift arrangement is a temporary substitute.

clue.text: Bang on about standing up to clergyman

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
a curate is an assistant clergyman

explanation.surface: Someone rails at length about confronting a vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bang on about' reads as nagging; 'Bang on' is the definition. 'standing up' reverses CA to AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Bang on is British slang for exactly right, precise.

clue.text: Trails ticked off in area popular with ramblers

indicators.note: off means awry, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Walking routes checked off in a region favoured by hikers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TRAILS TICKED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake District is a mountainous national park in Cumbria, England, famed for fell walking.

clue.text: Penetrating boundary one has to get rid of in' US

parts.note: something penetrating goes deep
in cricket a six is one type of boundary, the ball cleared over the rope

explanation.surface: A cricket shot that pierces the boundary is something to be discarded in America.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a six is a hit over the boundary rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To deep-six is American slang for to discard, from burial at sea six fathoms down.

clue.text: Gesture important to train drivers striking

definitions.meaning: a sign made to convey a message
the lights or arms beside the track that tell drivers to stop or go
notable or outstanding, as in a notable success

explanation.definitionFit: Signal means a gesture, a railway stop-go device, and as an adjective conspicuous.

clue.text: For recreation, these GIs do this in a tourist spot

definitions.text: do this in a tourist spot

indicators.note: re-creation, making again, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers on leave do this when visiting a famous attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For recreation' reads as leisure; as re-creation it rearranges THESE GIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To sightsee is to go round visiting places of interest.

clue.text: Retire gracefully, left out of lavish do

indicators.note: one thing taken out of another is removed from it

parts.note: a blowout is a lavish party or meal

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws with dignity, leaving the extravagant party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' takes L from BLOWOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To bow out is to withdraw or retire from a role.

clue.text: Killer of president: kick by horse

parts.note: to boot is to kick
H is slang for heroin, which is horse

explanation.surface: A president's assassin was kicked by a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' looks like an animal; it is slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: John Wilkes Booth assassinated US President Abraham Lincoln in 1865.

clue.text: Place in home I found for youngster having nightmares

indicators.note: to place one piece in another is to insert it

parts.note: being at home is being in
a cub is a young animal, or a young Scout

explanation.surface: Finding a foster home for a child who suffers bad dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place in' is the container signal; 'home' giving IN is a standard crossword equivalence (at home = in).
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi are demons said to lie on sleepers; the word also meant oppressive bad dreams.

clue.text: Give OTT performance in musical

definitions.meaning: to perform in an over-the-top way to attract attention
the Kern and Hammerstein stage show about a Mississippi riverboat

explanation.definitionFit: To show off is to showboat; the musical is set on a theatre riverboat.

clue.text: Babylonian god making odd use of beetle

indicators.note: using only the odd letters means first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Worshippers of an ancient deity make strange use of an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd use of' takes the first, third and fifth letters of BEETLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bel was the Babylonian title of the chief god Marduk, meaning lord.

clue.text: Rich, not finding husband an asset

indicators.note: not finding a letter means it is missing

parts.note: plush means rich or luxurious

explanation.surface: A wealthy man without a spouse is a good catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finding' removes H from PLUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage or benefit.

clue.text: Duty officer involved in transparent offshore investment, say (3,7) 23,101 Soluti

parts.note: a duty is a tax

indicators.note: one piece involved in another sits inside it

parts.note: sheer fabric is transparent
LT is short for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A customs officer caught up in a see-through offshore scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' is the container signal. The trailing '23,101 Soluti' is page text the OCR picked up, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax shelter is a scheme for reducing tax liability, offshore funds being one example.
